claims.explanation: JZL-184 is a monoacylglycerol lipase (MGLL/MAGL) inhibitor, and its selective cytotoxicity likely reflects dependence on MAGL-driven lipid signaling (2-AG, LPA, PGE2) in tumor cells. Lines with high MGLL expression and intact downstream endocannabinoid/lipid signaling would be most sensitive, while loss of PTEN or other lesions that uncouple this pathway may protect. The pattern is also consistent with a non-canonical off-target effect, as the virtual cell profile resembles chloroquine and calcium-channel blockers rather than pure MAGL inhibition.

features.basis: MAGL is the direct target; high expression predicts dependence and JZL-184 sensitivity (PMID 27767105)
PTEN loss is enriched in least-affected lines and may uncouple lipid/PI3K signaling required for MAGL-dependent killing
BRAF-mutant melanomas appear in the sensitive set, suggesting MAPK-driven lipid dependence
KRAS-mutant colorectal, pancreatic, and gastric lines are among the most killed, consistent with RAS-driven lipogenesis
TP53 mutation is common in sensitive lines but also in resistant lines, so it is a weak, non-specific marker
NF1 mutations appear in several least-affected lines, possibly reflecting alternative survival signaling
EGFR-mutant lung lines are split between sensitive and resistant, so this is weak evidence
ARID1A mutations appear in several sensitive lines, suggesting chromatin remodeling may influence lipid pathway dependence
KMT2D mutations are enriched in least-affected lines, possibly reflecting epigenetic buffering
PIK3CA mutations appear in several resistant lines, suggesting PI3K activation may bypass MAGL dependence
CDKN2A loss appears in resistant lines, though the mechanism is unclear
SMARCA4 mutations appear in resistant lines, possibly altering transcriptional response to lipid stress
